result.note: Tests India's fertiliser import dependence, stockpiles and gas prioritisation, plus the strait behind the Qatar LNG disruption.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's fertiliser supply position in March 2026:
items: West Asia accounts for roughly half of India's diammonium phosphate (DAP) and urea imports.
The government prioritised gas supplies to fertiliser plants, ensuring at least 70% of average consumption.
DAP inventories were lower than a year earlier.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: The third statement is wrong. DAP inventories were up 105% and urea inventories up 10.7% from a year earlier, giving India a healthy buffer. Most shipments need to arrive between March and May ahead of the June–July kharif planting surge.
questions.source: Urea and DAP inventories are up 10.7% and 105% respectively from a year ago.

questions.prompt: In March 2026, threats around which strait disrupted LNG shipments from Qatar to India, prompting the government to prioritise gas supplies to fertiliser plants?
questions.explain: Qatar's LNG shipments were disrupted by threats around the Strait of Hormuz amid the West Asia war. In response, the government ensured fertiliser plants receive at least 70% of their average gas consumption.
questions.source: after LNG shipments from Qatar were disrupted by Strait of Hormuz threats, which we covered here.
